question: What is the main goal of a rectal washout?

options.A: To measure the exact core body temperature
options.B: To administer liquid nutrition directly to the colon
options.C: To permanently cure chronic lower back pain
options.D: To completely cleanse the lower bowel using fluid cycles

explanation: Think of a rectal washout as a thorough internal clean. It uses repeated cycles of fluid to wash out stubborn stool and debris from the lower colon. You've got this! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h1)

question: How does a rectal washout mostly differ from a regular cleansing enema?

options.A: It uses larger fluid volumes and cycles to thoroughly wash the lower colon
options.B: It is used exclusively to treat severe upper respiratory infections
options.C: It is only performed by surgeons in the operating theatre
options.D: It relies entirely on oral medications rather than rectal tubes

explanation: While a normal enema gives a quick flush, a rectal washout uses back-and-forth filling and draining cycles for a much deeper clean. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h1)

question: Which children's condition often needs rectal washouts before surgery?
explanation: In Hirschsprung's disease, a part of the baby's bowel lacks the nerves to push stool out. Washouts are safely used to clear things out before surgery! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h2)

question: A patient has a stubborn, hard mass of stool that normal enemas can't shift. What procedure is best here?
explanation: When standard enemas aren't strong enough to break up severe blockages, a rectal washout provides the extra mechanical help needed. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h2)

question: When should you definitely NOT perform a rectal washout?

options.A: A stable history of controlled high blood pressure
options.B: Temporary loss of appetite for two days
options.C: Recent bowel surgery with an active anastomosis
options.D: Mild chronic constipation in an elderly adult

explanation: Never force fluid into a fresh surgical connection (anastomosis)! The pressure could cause it to break open, leading to dangerous leaks. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h3)

question: What is a major risk when using large amounts of plain tap water for a washout?

options.A: Permanent damage to the upper respiratory tract
options.C: Sudden spikes in systemic blood pressure
options.D: Rapid development of iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Plain water can pass through the bowel wall into the bloodstream, diluting vital body salts and causing a dangerous drop in sodium levels. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h3)

question: Which fluid is normally used for a washout to keep body salts balanced?
explanation: Normal saline is isotonic, meaning it matches body fluids and prevents dangerous shifts of water and salt across the bowel wall. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h4)

question: Why do we position the patient in the left lateral Sims' position for a rectal washout?

options.A: It follows the natural anatomical curve of the lower colon
options.B: It prevents the patient from falling asleep during the task
options.C: It completely stops normal peristaltic movement in the gut
options.D: It keeps the patient's head elevated above the heart level

explanation: The lower part of the colon curves down toward the left side, making the left lateral position the smoothest and easiest way to insert the tube. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h4)

question: Why should the fluid bag be kept at a low height during a washout?

options.A: To ensure a gentle, low-pressure gravity flow into the bowel
options.B: To speed up the chemical reaction of the irrigating fluid
options.C: To prevent the fluid inside the container from evaporating
options.D: To allow the nurse to check the temperature of the solution

explanation: Keeping the bag low prevents high pressure, protecting the delicate walls of the patient's intestine from accidental injury. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h5)

question: What should you do right away if your patient feels sharp belly cramps while you are running the fluid?

options.A: Stop the flow immediately until the cramp passes
options.B: Ignore the symptom as a normal expected reaction
options.C: Raise the fluid container higher to finish quickly
options.D: Push the rectal tube deeper into the sigmoid colon

explanation: Cramping means the bowel is filling up too fast! Always pause the flow and let the patient relax before starting again. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h5)

question: What is a common sign of vagal nerve irritation during rectal procedures?

options.A: Uncontrollable muscle spasms in the legs

explanation: The rectum is very close to the vagus nerve. If it gets irritated, it can cause the heart rate and blood pressure to drop suddenly, making the patient dizzy. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h6)

question: Why is checking the net fluid balance important after a rectal washout?

options.A: To calculate the exact caloric intake of the patient
options.B: To make sure the patient is not retaining excessive fluid
options.C: To verify the total operating room expenses for the day
options.D: To determine how much medication to give orally

explanation: Comparing how much fluid went in versus how much came out helps you make sure the patient isn't holding onto too much water. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h6)

question: What is the most crucial detail to write in your nursing notes after a washout?

options.A: The favorite food of the patient's family
options.B: The volume and appearance of the fluid returned
options.C: The weather conditions outside the hospital
options.D: The exact brand name of the lubricant used

explanation: Always document what came out! Recording the amount and look of the return proves that the procedure worked and was safe. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h7)

question: What should you do if you notice fresh, bright red bleeding from the rectum after a washout?

options.A: Report the finding to the physician immediately
options.B: Document it as a completely normal expected result
options.C: Administer a stronger oral laxative dose to the patient
options.D: Wait twenty-four hours to see if it stops on its own

explanation: Bright red blood means there might be a small injury or tear in the lining. Always let the doctor know right away so it can be checked. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h7)
